source: Hashimoto & Ohgushi 2023 original 120-larva 24h AAI split-leaf experimental table, Figshare 41146985, checksum verified
previous_audited_observations: 30 A.alcinous source leaf pairs; both loss=7, neither loss=16, AAI-only loss=6, control-only loss=1. Authors' strain label same for both halves in all 30 A.alcinous leaf pairs; four recorded source strain categories.
question: Does observed coincidence of larval loss within a source leaf persist after conditioning on shared original butterfly strain/batch labels, or can source-cohort heterogeneity explain it?
null: Within original source-strain groups, AAI-half and control-half author-coded loss indicators are independently assigned across leaf IDs conditional on the number of losses of each half in that same source group.
estimator: Exact convolution of stratum-wise hypergeometric overlap count distributions. Fixed stratum source leaf n, AAI-loss count and control-loss count. Compare observed total both-loss leaf pairs to the exact one-sided tail Pr(overlap>=observed), plus expected both-loss in each stratum.
scope: Secondary post-hoc sensitivity of dependence between two haphazard-loss indicators; not a causal AAI toxicity effect, not mechanistic leaf chemistry, not biological co-occurrence experiment.
quality_rules: No grouping invented from outcomes; use exact author strain string that was recorded before original assay outcomes.
Count native A.alcinous only for primary diagnostic; Sericinus has zero source-coded losses.
Do not remove leaf pairs with both deaths or assume losses independent.
Report unstratified Fisher exact and conditional source-strain results; do not select whichever is significant.
Cannot separate leaf handling, same maternal family, insect vigor, plant source or shared experimental contamination.
